subject: biology-2
question: Some protist groups carry **chloroplasts** wrapped in four membranes, including an outer membrane that resembles the cell membrane of a swallowed green alga. Which statement best explains how these chloroplasts arose?

options.text: Primary endosymbiosis, when a host cell engulfed a cyanobacterium that became the chloroplast.
The chloroplasts are free-living bacteria that swim in and out of the host cell each day.
Mitochondria converted into chloroplasts when oxygen became abundant.
Secondary endosymbiosis, when a host cell engulfed a protist that already carried a primary chloroplast.

explanation: A chloroplast from an engulfed cyanobacterium carries two membranes, so four membranes record a second engulfment in which a host cell swallowed a whole alga that already held a primary chloroplast. A describes only the first, two-membrane stage. B confuses organelles with free-living cells, and C is impossible because mitochondria never become chloroplasts.
